notes: Read SKILL.md in full (single-file skill). The skill describes zero-trust architecture: core principles, Cloudflare Access apps/policies/device posture via API and Terraform, an oauth2-proxy deployment with nginx ingress auth, Istio strict mTLS and AuthorizationPolicies, default-deny Kubernetes NetworkPolicies, an OPA/Rego access policy, implementation steps and troubleshooting.

Medium: the curl examples call the Cloudflare API with the user's ${CF_TOKEN} bearer token to create Access applications, policies and device-posture rules (SKILL.md:65-107), and the manifests apply mesh-wide STRICT mTLS and namespace default-deny policies that can block traffic if applied without matching allow rules. Acceptable because these act on the user's own Cloudflare account and cluster, credentials come from environment variables or Kubernetes Secrets (no hardcoded values), and IDs/domains are placeholders; roll out deny policies in a test namespace first and confirm with the user.

Related Skills (SKILL.md:433-435) link to sibling skills ../../../infrastructure/networking/service-mesh/, ../../hardening/kubernetes-hardening/ and ../vpn-setup/ as optional reading only. The Rego `step_up_required` rule is defined but not wired into `allow`.
